newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Arafat signs key trade deal with European Union.
newsitem.headline: Arafat signs key trade deal with European Union.

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat signed a lucrative trade agreement with the European Union on Monday, accepting the economic, political and moral responsibilities that came with it.
"This is very important for the Palestinian people," Arafat told a news conference after he signed the so-called interim association agreement with the EU.
"With this we accept the economic, political and moral significance of the agreement between Europe and the Palestinian people."

The agreement -- which offers reduced tariffs for Palestinian exports to the EU, enhanced economic cooperation and increased development -- strengthened the 15-nation bloc's position as the Palestinian entity's main foreign bankroller.
Arafat said however that any deal would amount to naught unless the Palestinian entity was better able to export its goods.
How can we have a country on the Mediterranean without a port? " he said. "How can we have an authority without an airport."
He complained that although an airport in the Palestinian authority had been completed for seven months, he still had to use an international forces terminal to move around.
Arafat also reiterated warnings that Israeli plans to resettle more Israelis on the the West bank posed a great threat to peace.
"Not one single house is to be added," he said. "Those are the terms of the peace accords."
Hans van Mierlo, the Dutch Foreign Minister speaking on behalf of the EU presidency, said he was sure a human rights clause in the agreement would be honoured by the Palestinians.
"We are convinced that Yasser Arafat will do all he can on human rights," Van Mierlo said in response to a question.

A major human rights group called on Saturday for the EU to press Arafat to stop alleged abuses by Palestinian security forces. Human Rights Watch urged van Mierlo to push Arafat to free more than 500 people being detained without charge, or charge and bring them to trial soon.
